items.summary: Google Cloud has announced the availability of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 within the Google Antigravity platform for its customers. Marialaura Garcia of Google Cloud and Rich Hyndman of Google Antigravity explained that these models allow developers to select the right tool for specific tasks, ranging from quick bug fixes to complex migrations. The new models integrate with Antigravity 2.0, the CLI, and IDE extensions for VS Code and JetBrains IntelliJ. Administrators can configure usage through existing Google Cloud Billing accounts on a pay-as-you-go basis, while developers can switch between models directly in the model picker to optimize for cost, latency, or reasoning capabilities.
items.title: Google Antigravity Adds Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 Models

items.summary: Anthropic is struggling to secure sufficient cloud capacity from major providers like AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which now view the company as a competitor. The firm is leasing its own data centers but worries about their reliability. Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year, with third-quarter revenue reaching $16.8 billion, up 45% from the previous quarter.
items.title: Anthropic Faces Cloud Capacity Shortages Amid Growth

items.summary: OpenAI announced the acquisition of Orchestra Bio, a four-year-old startup specializing in AI agents for biotech operations. While deal terms remain undisclosed, Orchestra had reportedly raised approximately $20 million by 2025 from investors including Andreessen Horowitz. OpenAI intends to integrate Orchestra's technology into its Rosalind model and Workbench tool to assist life sciences researchers. This move highlights a trend of major AI labs expanding into pharmaceutical software, though concerns persist regarding potential future competition.
items.title: OpenAI Acquires AI Biotech Startup Orchestra Bio to Expand Life Sciences Capabilities

items.summary: Google launched Personal Intelligence for Gemini in 2026, initially a paid feature now available to all users. The company is rolling out this optional feature to Android Auto and Google Built-in vehicles. Google states that providing context allows AI to generate better outputs, enabling users to focus on driving while the system accesses data from connected apps like Gmail and Calendar to formulate answers.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Personal Intelligence to Android Auto and Built-in Vehicles

items.summary: Google is launching Gemini Personal Intelligence on Android Auto, granting the AI assistant access to user data like Photos, Gmail, and Calendar. This opt-in feature allows for tailored responses based on personal context, such as upcoming flights or dietary restrictions. Google states that all processed information remains within its secure infrastructure and is not used to train foundational AI models. Users can toggle access for specific apps and delete stored memory items at any time.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini Personal Intelligence on Android Auto

items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman won a dismissal of a lawsuit brought by his sister, Ann Altman, who alleged sexual abuse between 1997 and 2006. A US district judge dismissed the case after Ann Altman refused to attend an independent medical examination. The Altman family stated Ann has mental health challenges and supported her financially, while Sam Altman denied the accusations. The case was filed on 6 January 2025.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Wins Dismissal of Sister's Lawsuit

items.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI are developing plans to share profits with the public before their stock offerings, aiming to address workforce disruptions. Anthropic announced it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, pending stockholder approval. While the fund might support nonprofits or specific populations, Anthropic stated it will not support lobbying. Experts welcome the move but urge caution regarding the companies' philanthropic wisdom.
items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Plan Wealth Sharing Ahead of IPOs

items.summary: Wall Street rose on Oct 20, led by the Dow Jones Industrial Average, as investors shifted focus to healthcare and value stocks. Technology stocks lagged amid concerns over AI spending costs. The S&P 500 gained 0.31% to 7,714.52 points, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.03%. Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors noted a rotation into sectors like healthcare as equity investors remained skeptical about the AI trade.
items.title: Wall Street Rises as Investors Rotate Into Healthcare Stocks

items.summary: Tri Pham, chief strategy and innovation officer at Tata Communications, warns that AI adoption stalls if network infrastructure is not flexible enough to support daily use. He notes that while companies move AI from testing to operations, traditional networks often limit their ability to run large projects. Citing a 2025 survey by International Data Corporation, Pham highlights that 94 per cent of companies face network limitations, with 650 global enterprise technology leaders surveyed. He argues that companies must prioritize network agility, ensuring data, computing power, and communications tools connect seamlessly. Tata Communications offers on-demand bandwidth solutions to help businesses scale network capacity according to actual data requirements rather than fixed plans.
items.title: Tata Communications Executive Warns Network Infrastructure Limits AI Adoption

items.summary: ALTK-Evolve demonstrates that learned memory allows an older, non-reasoning GPT-4.1 model to outperform frontier models on customer service tasks. By extracting behavioral guidelines from training attempts and appending them to the system prompt, the agent achieves a 67.5% Pass^4 score on retail tasks, surpassing all leaderboard entries as of October 12, 2026. The method improves accuracy and reliability without increasing conversation length, though it raises input token costs. Testing with GPT-5.5 confirms the approach benefits stronger models as well, pushing airline task performance to 82.0%.
items.title: Learned Memory Enables Older AI Models to Top Customer Service Benchmarks

items.summary: Hamlet, an AI platform for local government data, adopted Databricks Lakebase Postgres to enable engineers and AI coding agents to test changes against isolated branches of production data. CEO Sunil Rajaraman and team members noted that this approach eliminates the need for manual staging setup, which previously took 15 to 30 minutes per pull request. By allowing agents to run pipelines on specific data without touching the live environment, the team reduces preparation time and improves velocity while maintaining human approval for merges. The system indexes over 7,200 governing bodies across the U.S., helping developers and researchers track policy developments.
items.title: Hamlet Uses Databricks Lakebase for AI Testing

items.summary: Hugging Face has introduced TorchTPU, a native backend that allows PyTorch models to run directly on Google's Tensor Processing Units. This update eliminates the need for the previous PyTorch/XLA interface, enabling Transformers and Diffusers libraries to operate on TPUs with standard code. The new tool supports eager and compiled modes, distributed training, and integration with existing Hugging Face models. While the library test suite shows 96.5% of TPU tests passing, the team continues to address the remaining 3.5% of failures to improve stability and performance for users.
items.title: Hugging Face launches native TPU support for PyTorch

items.summary: The PHP security team warns administrators to prepare for emergency updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities, each rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, scheduled for release on Wednesday, October 21. Information about the flaws reportedly leaked ahead of the disclosure. While the team has not disclosed technical details, researchers at watchTowr confirm the vulnerabilities are real and affect PHP versions 5 through 8.
items.title: PHP Security Team Warns of Critical Flaws Ahead of Emergency Patches

items.summary: Meta removed the word "train" from its commercial terms of service following backlash from legal experts who warned the policy could allow endless website scraping. Although Meta clarified the changes applied only to ads and business products, experts told Nieman Lab the updates do not sufficiently protect users from invasive data collection. The policy is set to take effect on October 30.
items.title: Meta Removes Word Train From Commercial Terms Amid AI Backlash

items.summary: Presenter Shiona McCallum visited a semiconductor facility producing flexible chips. Canada's AI Minister spoke to the BBC regarding the technology. The report also covers drone usage for monitoring fire-damaged landscapes, with production credits given to Tom Quinn.
items.title: Shiona McCallum visits semiconductor plant and discusses drone technology

items.summary: A developer has released Battle Drones, a Real-Time Strategy game created primarily through prompts given to AI coding agents. The project, released on October 20, 2026, evolved from a basic prototype into a feature-rich experience with 3D graphics, multiple play modes, and audio-based multiplayer. The developer noted that early versions were not fun to play, but a specific prompt to 'Make it a LOT more fun' triggered a dynamic workflow that significantly improved gameplay balance and engagement. The final version includes 3D models, various maps, and features like AI-vs-AI battles and a random map generator, all built using TypeScript and Three.js without the developer writing most of the code.
items.title: Developer Shares Vibe-Coded RTS Game Built with AI Agents

items.summary: Zeabur announced its shutdown after a second security breach in two months, where attackers stole over 3.2 million environment variable records and data for 321,810 accounts. The company cited the recent failures and operational complexity as reasons for winding down services by the end of 2026.
items.title: Zeabur Shuts Down Following Second Security Breach

items.summary: Guardian US columnist Rebecca Solnit writes that Americans are increasingly opposing big technology companies and artificial intelligence. Citing surveys and activist groups, she notes widespread public anxiety regarding AI datacenters and surveillance tools. Solnit references specific opposition, including a march in San Francisco against Palantir and a New York City ban on AI for students. She highlights voices from Pope Francis and tech critics like Sherry Turkle who warn against the dehumanizing effects of algorithms. The article frames this movement as a defense of human agency, creativity, and democracy against what Solnit terms 'tech oligarchs' who ignore public will. She concludes by predicting that upcoming elections will serve as a referendum on this alignment between technology giants and political power.
items.title: Guardian Columnist Describes Growing Grassroots Resistance to Big Tech and AI

items.summary: Tesla is set to report third-quarter 2026 financial results on October 21, with Wall Street expecting flat revenue and a 10% drop in earnings per share compared to the prior year. While vehicle deliveries reached 486,532 units, exceeding analyst consensus, the company delivered more vehicles than it produced, indicating inventory reduction. Energy storage deployments fell short of estimates. Analysts anticipate operating margins will remain under pressure due to lower average selling prices and reduced regulatory credits, with free cash flow expected to remain negative as capital expenditures rise significantly.
items.title: Tesla Q3 2026 Earnings Preview Shows Flat Revenue and Falling Profits

items.summary: Edmunds tested the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC 400 4Matic EV, finding it drove 392 miles, surpassing its EPA estimate of 331 miles by 18%. The vehicle consumed 28.4 kWh per 100 miles, roughly 14% less than the official figure. Mercedes states the battery charges from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.
items.title: Mercedes-Benz GLC 400 EV Exceeds EPA Range Estimates in Testing

items.summary: Inflation rates in the United States remain high, with the Consumer Price Index showing a 3.7 percent rise over 12 months. Energy costs are a primary driver, with gasoline prices up 34.2 percent and fuel oil up 74.2 percent. Tim McDonnell of Semafor attributes this to the war in Iran, noting that geopolitical instability creates persistent vulnerability in the US economy. While domestic drilling offers some control, it cannot shield consumers from global price turmoil. Experts suggest a transition to renewable energy like solar and wind is necessary to reduce reliance on volatile fossil fuels and achieve energy independence.
items.title: High Energy Costs Drive U.S. Inflation Amid Global Volatility

items.summary: The American Petroleum Institute estimated that US crude oil inventories fell by 4.93 million barrels in the week ending October 16. This follows a larger drop of 11.12 million barrels the prior week. Commercial inventories excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve have lost over 56 million barrels in 27 weeks, though total crude remains only 5 million barrels below the start of the year. US production slipped to 13.679 million bpd, while Brent and WTI crude prices declined on the day.
items.title: API Reports US Crude Inventories Drop Amid SPR Draws

items.summary: The Mesa Grande Band of Diegueño Mission Indians, partnering with the Solar Electric Light Fund, installed solar and battery storage systems at three Tribal facilities. This marks the first public clean energy installation on the reservation, aiming to increase energy sovereignty. The systems are expected to generate approximately 60 MWh annually and save the Tribe at least $16,780 per year. Battery storage allows buildings to operate independently during common power outages. The project supports broader goals of housing development and community infrastructure.
items.title: Mesa Grande Tribe Completes Solar Storage Project for Energy Resilience

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that AI startup Anthropic recorded a net loss of over $80 billion in the first half of 2026, citing a draft IPO prospectus. The loss included $72 billion in accounting charges related to convertible notes. This compares to a $13 billion loss in the same period last year. Reuters also noted a 45% revenue rise to $16.8 billion in the third quarter.
items.title: Anthropic Reports Massive Net Loss in First Half of 2026

items.summary: A federal judge in Missouri dismissed a sexual abuse lawsuit filed by Sam Altman's sister in 2025. The case ended after she refused to attend a required medical examination. Altman denies the allegations, which claimed abuse occurred between 1997 and 2006. His lawyer stated the claims were untrue, while the sister's former attorney expressed continued belief in her.
items.title: Federal Judge Dismisses Sam Altman's Sister's Sexual Abuse Lawsuit

items.summary: The Liberty Justice Center filed a lawsuit challenging White House tariffs on Canadian goods, arguing the administration exceeded its authority under Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act. Representing Gellert Global Group, the group claims the levies caused immediate harm and violated legal limits on executive power. The case seeks to block tariff collection and establish that Congress, not the executive branch, holds tariff power.
items.title: Liberty Justice Center sues over Canadian tariffs

items.summary: The Delhi government launched a ₹104 crore pilot project targeting 40 locations to reduce PM2.5 and PM10 levels by 20% using new technologies. The one-year initiative involves private companies and startups, with daily air quality monitoring by sensors and an independent committee evaluating effectiveness.
items.title: Delhi Government Plans ₹104 Crore Pilot Project to Reduce Air Pollution

items.summary: CyberPulse reports a hacker named Siriusim claims to have leaked 3.75 lakh SBI records and 2,722 PDFs containing private customer data. CyberPulse warns of identity theft risks, though SBI has not confirmed the leak or system breach.
items.title: CyberPulse Reports SBI Data Leak Claim by Hacker Siriusim

items.summary: Super Micro Computer expects quarterly revenue between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, significantly exceeding analyst estimates of $15.23 billion. The company also forecasts gross margins of 12% to 12.5%, up from previous expectations. These results reflect strong demand for AI servers, contributing to an 11.3% rise in the company's shares.
items.title: Super Micro Reports Soaring Quarterly Revenue and Profit Margins Amid AI Boom

items.summary: The Trump administration has not yet loosened its control over Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the ownership structure remains unclear and may benefit homeowners. President Donald Trump previously considered selling government shares. Bessent warned that releasing the firms could spike mortgage rates, which are currently at their highest levels since November 2023.
items.title: Trump Administration Delays Release of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac

items.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration proposed a rule to protect New York City consumers from AI chatbot "doom loops." The regulation would require businesses to connect customers to human agents quickly if chatbots fail to fulfill requests. Violators face fines starting at $525. Mamdani stated that customer service cost-cutting should not come at New Yorkers' expense. The rule aims to ensure transparency and provide an easy off-ramp to human representatives.
items.title: Mayor Mamdani Proposes AI Chatbot Protection Rule for New York

items.summary: The author argues that capital supply determines the size of growth booms associated with automation, while task structure influences duration and wage evolution. Evidence shows that fixing the U.S. saving rate at 23% in 2025 reduces potential annual growth from 11.7% to 2.2%. The author suggests slow growth may reflect insufficient capital accumulation rather than technological bottlenecks, noting that automation raises the capital share, which increases the ten-year real yield from 5.1% to 13.6%.
items.title: Author argues capital accumulation drives automation growth

items.summary: Andy Burnham is set to approve the Jackdaw gasfield, a decision that signals the Labour government's commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry and risks conflict with climate campaigners and some Labour MPs. The approval, announced by Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh and Chancellor John Healey in Aberdeen, follows a year of deliberation regarding UK climate commitments. While officials argue the project does not violate manifesto pledges as it is not a new licence, critics contend it undermines green credentials. The field, operated by Shell and Equinor, is expected to supply around 2% of gas demand for roughly 10 years and account for 6% of North Sea gas production when fully operational.
items.title: Andy Burnham approves Jackdaw gasfield despite climate backlash

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that Anthropic could spend $750 billion on computing power before its IPO. The company recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, driven largely by accounting charges. Spending on computing capacity rose to nearly $9 billion in six months. The draft prospectus outlines agreements totaling around $450 billion over the next seven to 10 years, including contracts with Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft. Anthropic faces potential risks, including political opposition to data center construction in the US.
items.title: Anthropic May Spend $750B on Computing Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that US intelligence sharing regarding Russian missile attacks is functioning effectively following talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo. The discussions, which included US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, addressed early warning systems and Starlink access. While Zelensky expressed gratitude for the intelligence flow, he noted that Russia must now respond to peace proposals. Concurrently, Russian drone attacks continued, killing at least 10 people in Ukraine. US officials described the negotiations as productive, though unconfirmed reports suggest Patriot missile transfers remain pending. European leaders emphasized the need for joint resolution of the conflict.
items.title: Zelensky Confirms US Intelligence Sharing Works After Oslo Talks

items.summary: Italy's government is deploying 500 soldiers to Milan following protests against the cost of living that escalated into clashes, vandalism, and looting. Police detained 271 young people, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, after violent groups set bins ablaze and ransacked shops. The government, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, vows a firm response and plans to approve tougher security measures, including extending preventive detention for minors and banning gatherings for those deemed a threat. Meanwhile, similar unrest in France and Portugal has prompted travel advice and curfews in several European cities.
items.title: Italy Deploys 500 Soldiers Amid Protests and Looting

items.summary: SpaceX reported a ninefold increase in AI revenue to $US7.6 billion, boosting shares by 2.5%. This surge, alongside positive US stock finishes, is expected to lift the ASX. Analysts note the company's AI business now serves as its primary revenue driver.
items.title: SpaceX AI Revenue Surge Drives ASX Rise Expectations

items.summary: On October 20, Paris St Germain defeated Barcelona 4-2 in a Champions League match, securing the top spot in the standings. Liverpool and Manchester City also won their respective games. PSG players Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha, and Fabian Ruiz scored, while Barcelona's Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal each netted twice. Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3, and Manchester City defeated AEK Athens 5-1.
items.title: PSG Defeat Barcelona to Top Champions League Standings

items.summary: Interest in the Elizabeth Holmes fraud scandal surged following the announcement of the documentary You Can See Everything. Viewership for the Hulu series The Dropout jumped 186% in September and nearly doubled again in October. The film achieved record-breaking box office numbers and is expected to receive multiple Oscar nominations.
items.title: Documentary You Can See Everything Boosts The Dropout Viewership

items.summary: Townsville's Abbey Ellis scored 47 points in a WNBL victory over Adelaide, the most by an individual in 21 years. Ellis hit 16 of 24 field goals, including seven three-pointers. Townsville improved to 1-1 while Adelaide dropped to 0-2. Ellis joined league legends like Lauren Jackson in recording 47 points and six steals. Townsville coach Shannon Seebohm praised Ellis's bravery and defense.
items.title: Abbey Ellis Scores Record 47 Points in WNBL Victory

items.summary: Spotify announced in October 2026 that it excluded over 50 million AI-generated or spam tracks from its recommendations in 2026. The company also removed more than 75 million tracks for rule violations. Spotify stated these measures protect listeners and promote human artists while updating detection systems based on listener feedback and metadata.
items.title: Spotify Excludes 50 Million AI Tracks From Recommendations

items.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow interviewed William Taylor, former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine, regarding President Trump's recent moves to support Russia. The discussion contrasts these actions with past administrations and examines how current U.S. support for Ukraine differs from previous periods. NPR clarified that it does not accept money for coverage or interviews.
items.title: NPR Discusses Shift in U.S. Support for Ukraine with Former Ambassador

items.summary: Nigeria confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja involving a woman who arrived from Uganda, according to the Health Ministry. Authorities have traced 44 contacts. The case involves the Bundibugyo virus, which has caused thousands of infections and deaths. Health officials warn of a serious threat as the outbreak spreads across Africa, with Nigeria having previously recorded 20 cases.
items.title: Nigeria Confirms Ebola Case in Abuja Amid Regional Outbreak

items.summary: US President Donald Trump told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to make a deal with Russia, stating the US received nothing but grief and financial loss for its support. Trump expressed taxpayer fatigue regarding the conflict. These comments followed a meeting between Zelenskyy and a US delegation in Oslo, where the Ukrainian leader appeared more positive, citing constructive intelligence sharing and calling for peace.
items.title: Trump Urges Zelenskyy to Make Deal with Russia Amidst US Frustration

items.summary: Italy approved deploying 500 troops to Milan and enacted stricter security measures, including easier detention of minors and criminalizing violent participation in demonstrations. These actions followed violent clashes during fuel price protests that disrupted pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy, as reported by FRANCE 24.
items.title: Italy Deploys Troops and Tightens Security Laws Following Milan Clashes

items.summary: Spain's Guardia Civil rescued a family and their dogs from a flooded home in Oliva as heavy flooding affected the Valencia region. Footage shows an officer carrying a woman through floodwater while a man was led to safety. The family was transported out of the town in a Guardia Civil vehicle. Aerial images revealed large submerged areas near the coast with emergency crews continuing operations to reach trapped residents.
items.title: Guardia Civil Rescues Family and Dogs from Rising Floodwaters in Oliva

items.summary: Nigeria's Health Ministry confirmed the country's first known Ebola case in Abuja, involving a woman who arrived from Uganda. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate stated the patient exhibited symptoms on October 7 and was diagnosed on October 11. Authorities have traced 44 contacts and are implementing containment measures. The current outbreak, driven by the Bundibugyo strain, has surpassed 9,000 cases globally, primarily in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
items.title: Nigeria Confirms First Ebola Case in Abuja Amid Regional Outbreak

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Kharkiv to address strained US-Ukraine relations. Kyiv has complained that Washington is withholding vital defences while President Donald Trump courts Moscow, causing ties to reach new lows.
items.title: Zelensky Meets Witkoff Amid Deteriorating US-Ukraine Relations

items.summary: As the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) approaches its conclusion on December 31, 2026, uncertainty regarding the security of southern Lebanon is increasing. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has warned against a power vacuum should the force withdraw without a replacement. While the European Union has agreed to establish a new support mission, it is not intended to replace UNIFIL's peacekeeping role. The upcoming withdrawal highlights significant challenges for the Lebanese government, including economic dependence on international funding tied to Hezbollah's disarmament and the difficulty of tracking violations without an international military presence.
items.title: Lebanon Faces Uncertainty as UNIFIL Mandate Nears End

items.summary: Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and US counterpart Marco Rubio met in Mumbai to expand cooperation in energy, defence, and technology. They committed to concluding a trade deal soon, with Rubio noting they are 'as close as you can be without having an executed agreement.' The ministers discussed diversifying energy supplies and reducing reliance on Russia, ahead of upcoming meetings between PM Modi and President Donald Trump.
items.title: India and US Ministers Agree to Boost Defence and Energy Ties

items.summary: Three-month copper prices rose slightly to $14,353 a ton, marking a third session of tight trading. Prices have gained 55% since January 2025, despite a 0.5% drop in global demand to 27 million metric tons. Analysts note support from China's scrap shortage and inventory drawdowns, while tariff uncertainty and supply disruptions from Chile keep traders cautious.
items.title: Copper Prices Remain Stable Amid Tariff and Supply Concerns

items.summary: Gellert Global Group filed a lawsuit challenging President Donald Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian products, arguing the administration lacked legal authority under a 1930 trade law. The company seeks to halt enforcement and collect refunds with interest. This legal challenge follows trade negotiations that broke down, prompting the US to impose duties on billions of dollars of Canadian goods.
items.title: Gellert Global Group Sues Over Canadian Tariffs

items.summary: The Delhi High Court set aside a Central Information Commission order directing the Indian Air Force to disclose flight records of PM Narendra Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh. Justice Amit Mahajan ruled that revealing such details could compromise national security and the leaders' safety, rejecting the argument that redacting names would eliminate risks. The court affirmed that public funding for visits does not justify exposing security arrangements.
items.title: Delhi High Court Upholds IAF Refusal to Disclose PM Flight Records

items.summary: SpaceX reported Q3 revenue of $14. 6 billion, significantly exceeding analyst estimates of $12. 72 billion, according to LSEG data. The growth is primarily driven by Starlink and connectivity operations, which fund CEO Elon Musk's AI ambitions. While AI software offerings like Grok are expanding, they have not yet matched the traction of rivals such as OpenAI and Google. SpaceX generates most AI revenue by leasing data-centre computing capacity rather than relying on proprietary models. Investors are monitoring whether expanding into international markets and introducing cheaper subscription plans will impact average revenue per user over time.
items.title: SpaceX Q3 Revenue Surges 161% Driven by AI and Connectivity

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the United States and India are very close to finalizing a trade agreement, with only a few items remaining. Speaking in Mumbai, Rubio expressed optimism that the pact would be in place shortly, noting that the State Department is heavily involved in the process. The article provides context on bilateral trade figures for FY26, showing a 6.5% rise in overall trade to $140.76 billion. Rubio also discussed India's role in the Quad, defence cooperation, and energy diversification, mentioning potential Venezuelan crude oil processing capabilities at Reliance Industries in Jamnagar. His visit to India is scheduled to conclude on 22 October.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Says Trade Deal With India Is Very Close

items.summary: The government has amended SEZ rules to allow units to return rejected goods to the Special Economic Zone under specific conditions, such as changes in fashion or market conditions. The notification requires identity verification, evidence of no benefits availed by the buyer, and maintenance of a separate inventory. Additionally, a new relief measure allows eligible SEZ units to sell goods in the Domestic Tariff Area at concessional duty rates for one year, effective from April 1, 2025, with a cap on the total value of goods cleared.
items.title: Government Expands Conditions for SEZ Goods Return to Domestic Market

items.summary: Shipping data from Kpler and LSEG indicate Russian diesel cargoes are returning to Turkey and Brazil following the lifting of Moscow's export ban. At least two tankers signaled voyages to these destinations in recent days as the ban was removed.
items.title: Russian diesel cargoes return to Turkey and Brazil after export ban lift

items.summary: In June 2016, the Classen-Steubing family agreed to sell 204 acres of historic ranchland in northern San Antonio to the city. The deal prevents up to 3,500 homes from being built and protects the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone. Officials approved the initial 165-acre purchase for approximately $6.35 million, with the remaining 39 acres subject to a separate funding decision later in 2017.
items.title: San Antonio Family Sells Ranch Land for Park and Water Protection

items.summary: Delhi Police transferred a second case against jailed Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to the Crime Branch. The move follows their alleged trespassing at Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Party founder Abhijeet Dipke described the leaders as real decision-makers and announced a protest pause until Diwali.
items.title: Delhi Police Transfer CJP Leaders' Cases to Crime Branch Amid Protest Agitation

items.summary: The Maharashtra Transport Department conducted a special inspection drive between October 5 and 17 to target private vehicles registered outside the state but used locally. Officials found 475 vehicles violating rules, seized 12, and recovered ₹24.09 lakh in fines. The action addresses concerns about tax evasion through out-of-state registration, aiming to ensure vehicles regularly used in Maharashtra pay applicable state taxes.
items.title: Maharashtra Transport Department Recovers Fines From Out-Of-State Vehicles

items.summary: On October 20, 2026, Directorate of Revenue Intelligence officials at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport busted a gold smuggling syndicate. Officers seized 2,317 grams of 24-karat gold valued at Rs 3.47 crore. Five individuals, including two passengers and two handlers, were arrested and remanded to judicial custody after allegedly intercepting the consignment.
items.title: DRI Busts Gold Smuggling Syndicate at Mumbai Airport

items.summary: Hollywood actor Steve Buscemi supports Friends of Firefighters, a nonprofit he does not found but serves on its advisory council. The organization, established in 2001 by Nancy Carbone, offers free, confidential mental health services to FDNY firefighters and their families. According to its website, by 2024 the charity delivered more than 4,200 counselling sessions annually. Buscemi, a former firefighter who returned to the service after the September 11 attacks, uses his public profile to raise awareness for the group's work addressing trauma and stress among first responders.
items.title: Steve Buscemi Supports Charity Providing Mental Health Services to Firefighters

items.summary: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge requested the RSS to obtain formal permission for its Vijayadashami route marches on October 25. Citing police concerns over security and public resources, Kharge stated that mere notification does not constitute approval. He noted the RSS planned 562 marches involving 2,21,963 participants. The RSS maintains registration is not mandatory for all activities.
items.title: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge seeks formal permission for RSS Vijayadashami marches

items.summary: Students from Krantikari Yuva Sangathan burned a 20-feet tall effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi's Model Town park during Dussehra celebrations. Police detained several activists briefly for occupying public space without permission. The group claimed the act was a form of free speech to protest alleged irregularities in electoral roll revisions. Police stated they removed protesters and detained 10-12 individuals before releasing them within hours.
items.title: Students Burn Effigy of Election Commissioner in Delhi Protest

items.summary: Uddhav Thackeray criticized the Maharashtra government's handling of the attack on actor Tiger Shroff, questioning why officials did not meet the injured actor immediately. Thackeray alleged the Bishnoi gang, which claims a network of 70,000 members, is responsible and challenged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to confront the gang leaders. While the gang claimed responsibility, police have not verified the assertion. Thackeray also condemned the attackers for surviving the incident.
items.title: Uddhav Thackeray Challenges Fadnavis Over Tiger Shroff Attack Response

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the upcoming film 'The Ramayana', starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, will be made tax-free in the state. Speaking at Dussehra celebrations in Kolkata, Adhikari noted that the film joins other projects like 'The Kashmir Files' in receiving this status. The event, organized by Salt Lake Sanskritik Sansad, also featured tributes to a recent tragedy at a local Durga Puja pandal. Cast members and producers expressed their happiness at the announcement and the festival's theme of good triumphing over evil. Part 1 of the film is scheduled for release on November 5, 2026.
items.title: West Bengal CM Declares Ramayana Film Tax-Free
